STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — Amid recent shooting incidents and other security concerns in schools, Education Secretary Sonny Angara yesterday expressed his support for the passage of the Comprehensive School Safety Act that gives priority to school safety and well-being of learners.
The Department of Education (DepEd) said Angara showed his support to Sen. Bam Aquino at the Senate on Wednesday as the senator proposed the Comprehensive School Safety Act.
The bill seeks to institutionalize DepEd’s ongoing learner protection initiatives into permanent law, ensuring that critical safety protocols remain funded and sustained.
The legislative push follows nationwide concerns after shooting incidents at the San Jose National High School in Tacloban and the Ateneo de Zamboanga University.
The proposed Comprehensive School Safety Act establishes a three-pillar framework: prevention, response and recovery.
Under prevention, the bill mandates risk identification and safety training for parents, teachers and student leaders.
Response outlines emergency protocols, communication networks, active attack safety drills and coordination with authorities.
The recovery phase ensures psychosocial support, trauma-informed care and structured return-to-school plans.
The DepEd is expediting the recruitment of 10,000 school counselor associates nationwide, aiming to deploy them by year-end.
La Salle security
A student’s message on an online group chat with fellow students that he is a shooter disrupted classes at La Salle Greenhills in Mandaluyong City yesterday.

In a Facebook post, the school aid classes from preschool to Grade 12, including International Baccalaureate and Alternative Education programs, were conducted online as a precautionary measure. – Emmanuel Tupas

articles.title: Sweeping DPWH budget reforms set
articles.summary: There will be a sweeping overhaul in the budget submission process of the Department of Public Works and Highways, whose total project count for next year will be slashed by more than half, DPWH…

blocks.text: DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon also warned DPWH district engineers (DEs) that signing off on unvetted or “defective, anomalous” projects could land them in jail.
DPWH via Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — There will be a sweeping overhaul in the budget submission process of the Department of Public Works and Highways, whose total project count for next year will be slashed by more than half, DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon said yesterday.
Dizon also warned DPWH district engineers (DEs) that signing off on unvetted or “defective, anomalous” projects could land them in jail.

Highlighting a complete departure from “old budget habits” that allowed billions in public funds to be squandered on poorly planned infrastructure projects, Dizon said the DPWH is imposing a strict “no plan, no budget” policy across all regional and district offices.
“The old ways of budgeting are over,” he told reporters yesterday during his inspection of flood control and infrastructure projects at the EDSA Balintawak Cloverleaf area in Quezon City.

“We no longer accept project entries that consist of just a line-item title and a price tag. Projects must originate from community needs and satisfy complete prerequisite engineering requirements before entering the budget.”

Under the newly instituted accountability framework, DEs are required to personally sign certification documents guaranteeing that submitted projects have secured right-of-way acquisitions, detailed engineering designs and complete programs of work.
Dizon cautioned field officials against blindly approving lump-sum or unverified proposals, warning that their personal signatures will serve as primary evidence in criminal proceedings.

“If a DE signs off on a project and it turns out to be defective, anomalous, or ghost infrastructure, they are automatically held accountable,” he warned. “I will bring their signed certifications directly to the National Bureau of Investigation or the Ombudsman. It will be an open-and-shut case, and corrupt district engineers will go straight to prison.”

To enforce strict quality control and eliminate bloated, uncoordinated civil works, Dizon said the DPWH drastically pared down its project portfolio from 26,000 projects in previous budget cycles down to 11,000 highly targeted national projects.
Dizon reiterated that every approved project must carry written concurrence from the concerned local government unit to ensure alignment with local drainage and traffic master plans.
“While these reforms aren’t entirely foolproof, they create a formidable shield against the systemic corruption of the past,” Dizon added. “We will remain vigilant in guarding the public coffers.”

articles.title: P7.2 trillion budget bill for 2027 filed
articles.summary: The bill containing the government’s spending plan worth P7.2 trillion for fiscal year has been formally filed before the House of Representatives.

blocks.text: The bill serves as the legislative equivalent of the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP) that Malacañang annually submits to Congress.
Philstar.com / Irra Lising
MANILA, Philippines — The bill containing the government’s spending plan worth P7.2 trillion for fiscal year has been formally filed before the House of Representatives.
House committee on appropriations chairperson Mikaela Suansing said she has formally filed House Bill 10858 or the 2027 General Appropriations Bill.
The bill serves as the legislative equivalent of the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP) that Malacañang annually submits to Congress.
“We are working to ensure the careful scrutiny of the national budget for the year 2027,” Suansing said.
The House of Representatives started the committee-level budget deliberations last week.
After the committee, the bill will then be deliberated at the plenary.

The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) earlier said the Department of Education (P976 billion) and Department of Public Works and Highways (P644 billion) were among the agencies with the largest allocations in the proposed budget for next year.
Senate conducts budget hearing

The Senate yesterday led the Development Budget Coordination Committee (DBCC) hearing into the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027, with economic managers and senators talking about the need to tame inflation and end corruption following the flood control mess.

Monetary and fiscal managers from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), Department of Finance, and DBM were grilled by the senators about the rising cost of living and the global headwinds – like regional wars and oil price shocks – that affect economic growth.

Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian questioned BSP Governor Eli Remolona about the capacity of the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC), which Remolona chairs, in flagging suspicious bank flows due to corruption.

Sen. Francis Pangilinan pointed toAMLC’s failure to flag Syms Construction flood control contractorSally Santos’ transaction at Landbank in cashing out an alleged P457 million kickback to dismissed district engineer Brice Hernandez, a finding of last year’s explosive Blue Ribbon flood control inquiry.
Remolona and other BSP officials said the AMLC is undergoing an AI project to digitize its monitoring of millions of covered and suspicious transactions flagged by and reported to the council.
Sen. Panfilo Lacson said he led last year’s augmentation of P162.9 million for the AMLC budget in 2026 for this AI project.
Sen. Camille Villar raised concern over the decline in the country’s gross domestic product growth rate, from 2.8 percent in the first quarter to 2.3 percent in the second quarter.
Remolona said tight spending as a result of the flood control mess contributed to the economic slowdown.

Asked by Sen. Risa Hontiveros about the economic “have-nots” that contributed to the slowdown, Remolona said the country has to diversify its oil supply and to get into the AI sector, as he cited the Pax Silica manufacturing hub as a welcome initiative.

The Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) and the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA) have asked lawmakers for an additional P4 billion for migrant worker assistance programs in the 2027 budget, citing the continuing Middle East conflict and the need to maintain sufficient resources for the repatriation and assistance of OFWs.
The 2027 NEP provides P7.726 billion for the DMW and P4.349 billion for OWWA. – Marc Jayson Cayabyab, Christine Boton

articles.title: Teachers’ group slams P3.34 billion budget cut for SUCs
articles.summary: The Alliance of Concerned Teachers yesterday condemned the P3.34-billion slash in the budget for state universities and colleges or SUCs under the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP), while P10.8…

blocks.text: Out of 116 SUCs nationwide, 49 will suffer direct budget slashes while seven others will receive nominal increases of less than one percent.
Ramon Efren Lazaro

MANILA, Philippines — The Alliance of Concerned Teachers (ACT) yesterday condemned the P3.34-billion slash in the budget for state universities and colleges or SUCs under the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP), while P10.8 billion was allocated for confidential and intelligence funds or CIF.

In a statement, ACT chairperson Ruby Bernardo said that while the SUCs suffer budget cuts, P10.8 billion was allocated for CIFs – with P4.56 billion, or 44.9 percent of the total CIF, for the Office of the President alone.
Out of 116 SUCs nationwide, 49 will suffer direct budget slashes while seven others will receive nominal increases of less than one percent.
“The cutbacks in education are directly depriving the young Filipinos of their rights to education,” Bernardo said.

ACT said the University of the Philippines System bears the single largest budget slash, losing nearly P2.95 billion – a move that would directly cripple funding for the Philippine General Hospital, which is the country’s premier government tertiary medical facility.
Specialized institutions such as the Philippine Normal University and Polytechnic University of the Philippines also face hefty cuts with P394.9 million and P291.8 million, respectively.
ACT asked lawmakers to immediately reject all proposed budget cuts, and fully restore the P3.34-billion reduction across all 49 affected SUCs.
The teachers’ group noted that the Department of the Interior and Local Government was given a P22-billion budget increase in the NEP, of which P16 billion would go to the Philippine National Police.

articles.title: BOC chief vows zero tolerance for agri smuggling
articles.summary: Customs Commissioner Ariel Nepomuceno has assured farmers that the agency will remain relentless in its fight against agricultural smuggling, emphasizing that protecting local producers, securing…

blocks.text: Customs Commissioner Ariel Nepomuceno speaks to farmers during a recent event
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — Customs Commissioner Ariel Nepomuceno has assured farmers that the agency will remain relentless in its fight against agricultural smuggling, emphasizing that protecting local producers, securing national borders, and ensuring proper government revenue collection are among the bureau’s top priorities.

Addressing members of the Magsasaka party-list and farmer leaders from Pampanga, Bataan, Aurora, Tarlac, Zambales, and Nueva Ecija, Nepomuceno acknowledged the damaging impact of smuggling on the livelihoods of farmers and fisherfolk across the country.

The Customs chief stressed that while the challenges confronting the agriculture sector extend beyond smuggling, the bureau remains committed to fulfilling its mandate through stronger border protection and stricter enforcement against customs fraud and illicit trade.
Nepomuceno also underscored President Marcos’ directives to strengthen revenue collection, minimize corruption, and modernize the Bureau of Customs.
He noted that the BOC has surpassed its revenue collection target by more than P11 billion, proving that reforms and efficient revenue generation can go hand in hand.

According to the commissioner, every successful effort to stop smuggling not only protects legitimate businesses and local producers but also ensures that government revenues intended for public programs and services are properly collected.
Reforms in the bureau have just started and this will be carried out over the long haul, he said.
He assured farmers of his continued support, saying he is on their side.

The gathering was attended by Magsasaka party-list chairman and former representative Argel Joseph Cabatbat, DIWA party-list chairman and former representative Michael Aglipay, Vice Mayor Allan Policarpio representing Mayor Michael Galang, and various farmer leaders from Central Luzon.

A highlight of the gathering was the approval of a motion conferring upon Nepomuceno the distinction of honorary member of Magsasaka, in recognition of his support for farmers and commitment to combating agricultural smuggling.

articles.title: Palace: No FB ban for now; Meta cooperating with government
articles.summary: The government is not banning Facebook for now, but is pushing for clearer FB rules on eliminating online content that promotes disinformation and encourages violence.

blocks.text: Palace press officer Claire Castro told a media briefing last Tuesday that the administration is open to banning Facebook and gaming applications following concerns about disinformation and the rising cases of deadly school violence.
AFP
MANILA, Philippines — The government is not banning Facebook for now, but is pushing for clearer FB rules on eliminating online content that promotes disinformation and encourages violence.

Palace press officer Claire Castro told a media briefing last Tuesday that the administration is open to banning Facebook and gaming applications following concerns about disinformation and the rising cases of deadly school violence.
The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center proposed the ban days after the shooting incident at the Ateneo de Zamboanga, which claimed the lives of two persons.
Speaking to reporters yesterday, Castro said Facebook has been responsive to the government’s efforts to immediately take down “fake news.”

“Facebook is not difficult to deal with and it doesn’t mean that if other social media platforms are not responsive, all of them would be banned. That is not what the President and our administration wants,” she said.

“But this is also a signal for other violators, especially the gaming apps that we know affect our youth and can cause violence. So that is what we want to relay because even if the President is open (to a ban), based on the latest information, our government does not have much problem with Facebook,” she added.

Castro urged other social media platforms to work with the government to prevent the spread of false information and violent content. She revealed that Information and Communications Technology Secretary Henry Aguda is set to travel to Singapore to meet with regional executives of Meta and discuss ways to immediately get rid of violent and false posts.

articles.title: DILG wants PNP access to homes of legal gun owners
articles.summary: The Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) has proposed allowing police access to inspect homes of owners of lawfully issued firearms to check procedures for safekeeping.

blocks.text: Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla on September 1, 2025.
STAR / Miguel De Guzman

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) has proposed allowing police access to inspect homes of owners of lawfully issued firearms to check procedures for safekeeping.
Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla yesterday suggested amending guidelines on the handling of government-issued guns amid recent fatal school shooting incidents that involved such weapons.
In his proposal, Remulla said firearm owners will be informed ahead of time about the inspection and they would provide a checklist and reminders on proper safekeeping practices.
He admitted that such a proposal might “upset some people” but reminded them that owning and carrying a gun is only a privilege.
He pointed out that in both cases of the recent school shootings in Tacloban and Zamboanga, the safekeeping of the guns was not in standard procedure.
In the Tacloban incident, a policewoman owned the government-issued gun used by one of the shooters, her nephew.
Meanwhile, the guns used in the Ateneo de Zamboanga University were owned by the father of the shooter, who was a Bureau of Customs personnel.
Remulla also urged Congress to repeal Republic Act 8294 or the so-called Robin Padilla law, which reduced penalties for illegal possession of firearms and made it a bailable offense.
However, he acknowledged that the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology could need additional funds to enhance their facilities if the law is repealed.
“Loose firearms in this country are prevalent. And if we catch them, it will be non-bailable, so we will need more room in our jails,” he said.

articles.title: Flood kills over 200 in Nepal; Pinoy among 1,300 missing
articles.summary: A Filipino was among hundreds reported missing as rescue teams searched on Thursday along the Nepal-China border after a catastrophic and deadly torrent of floods and mud swept through several…

blocks.text: DEVIGHAT – A Filipino was among hundreds reported missing as rescue teams searched on Thursday along the Nepal-China border after a catastrophic and deadly torrent of floods and mud swept through several communities following a glacier collapse.
The disaster left at least 273 people dead and more than 1,300 missing, including foreigners and pilgrims, and displaced hundreds of people across the Himalayan region.
Videos of the tragedy showed the flood swallowing up people as they tried to escape, and destroying buildings and bridges.
On Thursday, drone footage from Nepal showed the scale of the destruction.

The region’s steep valleys are economic lifelines and travel corridors, but are precarious when disaster strikes. Images showed what appeared to be the second floors of buildings in Nuwakot slathered in mud after the torrent rushed by. Debris hung from tree branches and wires, vehicles were buried and some stunned survivors were caked in mud. The floods halted travel in some areas.
There was little time for anyone to flee.
A Filipino was among the travelers missing after the deadly flash flood in the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers, the Nepal Tourism Board reported Thursday.
The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) said there are 128 reported Filipinos in Nepal, most of them women married to Nepalese and 18 of them migrant workers.

DFA spokesperson Analyn Ratonel said the Philippine embassy in New Delhi, which is mandated to represent the Philippines in Nepal, and the Honorary Consulate General of the Philippines in Kathmandu, Nepal, are actively monitoring the situation in parts of northern Nepal that had been hit by massive flash floods.
“The Embassy and the Consulate General are coordinating with Nepali authorities to determine whether there are affected Philippine nationals and provide emergency rescue or assistance,” Ratonel said.

The village of Soley in Nuwakot, with about 25 homes, was virtually wiped out, said Nirajan Paudyal, a Kathmandu-based journalist whose parents and other relatives live there. Desperate for information, he traveled to the area on Thursday for news of his family.
“There is no update till now. I fear there won’t be any update,” Paudyal said.
The Himalayan mountain range spans several countries in South Asia and has many of the world’s highest peaks and remaining glaciers.

The steep slopes and the lush valleys below the Himalayan mountain range are especially vulnerable to flooding and landslides, and extreme weather events. Melting glaciers have become more common because of warming because of human-caused climate change.
Researchers in Kathmandu found earlier this year that glaciers across the Hindu Kush Himalaya region are melting faster, with ice loss rates doubling since 2000.
The disaster has left at least 270 dead and 826 people missing in Nepal, and three dead and 558 missing in Tibet, authorities said.
Nepalese officials said that dozens of bridges were destroyed and nearly 40 kilometers of roads were damaged, complicating search efforts.
The Nepalese army has rescued more than 100 people from flood-affected areas through helicopter operations on Thursday morning, army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet said.

At least eight foreign nationals were airlifted to the country’s capital, Kathmandu, he said, adding that army teams also evacuated people trapped inside facilities linked to the Trishuli hydropower project.
Rescuers found bodies hundreds of kilometers downstream from the disaster zone in Chitwan district. Dozens of injured people have been transported to Kathmandu for advanced medical care.

Bishal Kumar Bhandari, chairman of the Nepal Red Cross Society, said they have shifted focus from rescue to large-scale relief operations in the flood-hit districts. He said that around 1,200 people were displaced from at least three villages.

In Tibet, a mudslide that struck near the land border crossing of Gyirong Port on Wednesday left mud in the surrounding areas more than 1.52 meters (5 feet) deep on average, with some road sections exceeding 2 meters (6 feet), Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported. Roads leading to the port were all damaged, while secondary collapses or landslides might occur as rain continued in the area, it added.
Chinese authorities deployed a large military transport aircraft to send a team to the region, and the country’s premier, Li Qiang, arrived in Gyirong on Thursday to direct rescue efforts.
Further, Chinese authorities are warning that a barrier lake, which formed at the confluence of Tsogyal River and the Purupqiangzangbu, is overflowing and may burst.

According to Nepal’s Tourism Board, 517 of the missing people in the country were foreigners and 178 of them were from India, and some were likely there on a pilgrimage to Mt. Kailash in Tibet, a sacred site for Hindus.

The site, however, drew tourists from all over the world. More than 60 of the missing in Nepal were from the US and the rest were from 30 other countries, ranging from Ukraine and the UK to South Africa and Japan, the Tourism Board said.

Indian spiritual guru and the head of the Isha Foundation, Sadhguru Jaggi Vasudev, said on X that 77 people from one of his pilgrimage groups to Mt. Kailash were caught in the flash floods at the immigration office at the Nepal-China border.

A visibly emotional Sadhguru said in a video that the group included foreign nationals from various countries. He said that there was no official information on the whereabouts of those who were at the immigration office, including 22 US nationals.
“Looking at the scale of destruction, it looks bad. The same building where we were for the immigration just a week ago, that entire building is washed away,” Sadhguru said.

In addition, China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Lin Jian said that nearly 100 Chinese citizens were missing on the Nepal side. He said that according to preliminary information, 260 of those missing in Tibet were foreigners.
Glacier collapse

The USGS later updated its analysis to say the seismic event it measured was a magnitude 5.2 glacier collapse that sent debris flowing downstream with catastrophic impact on communities. It said its determination was based on data from nearby seismic stations, long period seismic waves and satellite imagery, and that no earthquake had occurred.
Climate experts at the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development said an avalanche from a glacier likely caused Wednesday’s flash flood.

“Hydrological observations indicate the exceptional speed and magnitude of the flood wave,” they said in an emailed statement, noting that water levels at one point on the Trishuli river rose by as much as 9 meters (27 feet) over half an hour.
The Lhende Khola River, a tributary of the Bhotekoshi, had maximum flooding, they said.

The disaster in Nepal and Tibet is not a one-off. The increasingly unstable Himalayan ice system threatens communities, infrastructure and water supplies across one of the world’s most densely populated regions.

The region saw similar flash floods in August 2025, when a glacial lake in Tibet overflowed because of high temperatures. Nine people were killed, and critical infrastructure, including a bridge connecting Nepal and China, was damaged.
Marcos calls for prayers
In Manila, President Marcos asked for prayers for the communities hit by the flash floods in Nepal as the Philippine government continues to monitor the situation in the disaster-struck areas.

“His (Marcos) message is he was saddened by the incident and let us continue to pray for the improved condition of the people affected by the calamity in Nepal,” Palace press officer Claire Castro said in a media briefing yesterday.
In an X post, Marcos joined other world leaders in expressing grief over the flash flood in Nepal.
“The Philippines extends its deepest condolences to our friends in Nepal and to all those affected by the deadly flash flood yesterday,” the President said.
“Our deepest sympathies go out to those who lost family, loved ones and friends. Please accept our most heartfelt prayers for strength in this difficult time,” he added.

articles.title: Detained, at large, on leave senators decline salaries
articles.summary: Senators who are detained, at large or on leave have declined to receive their salaries since missing their on-site duties, according to Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian.

blocks.text: Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian
AFP / Jam Sta Rosa
MANILA, Philippines — Senators who are detained, at large or on leave have declined to receive their salaries since missing their on-site duties, according to Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian.
“Those who are detained and at large voluntarily declined,” Gatchalian said in a chance interview at the Senate yesterday.

One of them is Sen. Loren Legarda, who has missed attending Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial this month since the ombudsman announced a preliminary investigation over her and her son’s alleged involvement in ghost solar farm projects.
Gatchalian said Legarda, who is overseas, has extended her medical leave and declined receiving her salary.
“It’s a very personal issue. I’m aware of her ailment. Even prior to this, we were personal friends as well and she said she has a serious medical issue,” said Gatchalian.
“After she filed her medical leave she already declined her salary. We’ve instructed the accounting department and payroll department to suspend her salary,” he added.
There is no word when Legarda would return from her medical leave.
“I have no idea but she has to take her health seriously,” Gatchalian said.
Senators’ salaries which are not received by the principal can be converted as savings, Gatchalian said.
“The Senate can declare it as savings and use it for something else,” Gatchalian said.
Other senators currently absent at the Senate are Ronald dela Rosa, who is at large, and Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta, who are detained.

Dela Rosa has been in hiding since the International Criminal Court (ICC) ordered his arrest for the crimes against humanity case he faces with former president Rodrigo Duterte as a result of their bloody drug war.
Estrada is serving his 90-day suspension pending the litigation of his plunder case for allegedly receiving P573 million in kickbacks from anomalous flood control projects.
Marcoleta is also detained for plunder over an allegedly undeclared P75 million campaign funds for his 2025 senatorial bid.
Gatchalian said he is monitoring the situation of Estrada, who was taken to a hospital in San Juan on Wednesday after suffering a meniscus tear on his left knee.

articles.title: Jellyfish force partial shutdown of French nuclear plant
articles.summary: It is the second consecutive year that jellyfish has forced the closure of the Gravelines power station in northern France.

blocks.text: A massive influx of jellyfish has led to the partial shutdown of a nuclear reactor in northern France.

Two of Gravelines nuclear power station's six units were shut down on Wednesday and Thursday because of the presence of jellyfish in the seawater filtration system, which is used for cooling, Électricité de France (EDF) said.
A third unit has been shut down since 10 August due to the same issue, while a fourth has been closed for an inspection.
Gravelines, one of the country's biggest nuclear power stations located between Dunkirk and Calais in the Hauts-de-France region, was also closed last August because of jellyfish in its filters.
EDF said that units three, four and six were now shut.

Unit three had only been reconnected to the grid on 18 August after the first wave of jellyfish earlier this month, the company said, while units one and two were also operating at reduced power as a preventative measure.
Gravelines' six units each produce 900 megawatts of power. The station is cooled from a canal connected to the North Sea.
Several species of jellyfish are native and can be seen around the coast when the waters are warm.
Jellyfish are at their most active in the warmer months. Hot weather increases plankton levels at the water's surface, drawing jellyfish up, experts say.
Measures have been implemented to try to prevent jellyfish infiltration, including a partnership with fishermen who capture and release them further offshore, according to French outlet Ici.
There have been similar issues at other nuclear stations, including at the Torness plant in Scotland in 2011 and Sweden's Oskarshamn plant in 2013, but such cases are rare.

articles.title: San Miguel remits ₱78 billion to government for Manila airport deal
articles.summary: The private operator of the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) has remitted ₱78 billion to the government and invested nearly ₱7 billion in modernization since taking over the country’s main…

blocks.text: The private operator of the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) has remitted ₱78 billion to the government and invested nearly ₱7 billion in modernization since taking over the country’s main gateway in 2024.
In a statement, New NAIA Infrastructure Corp. (NNIC) said the ₱78 billion in remittances represents its payments under its concession agreement for the airport as of Aug. 15.
This includes the ₱30-billion upfront payment, an annual ₱2-billion payment, and 82.16 percent of gross airport revenues under the revenue-sharing arrangement.
To recall, NNIC secured the contract to operate NAIA after submitting the highest bid amount and revenue share.

“This is what the concession was designed to do: generate substantial and continuing revenues for government that can help support public services and infrastructure, while bringing in private sector resources to improve the airport,” said NNIC President Ramon Ang.

NNIC, a consortium led by Ang’s San Miguel Corp. (SMC), is expected to remit ₱36 billion annually, or more than ₱900 billion in revenues to the government over the course of its entire concession period.
The current concession of NNIC runs for 15 years, with an option to extend it for another 10 years.

As part of its concession, the private operator has committed to invest ₱170.6 billion to rehabilitate and modernize NAIA. Nearly two years in, it has already spent around ₱6.8 billion, or four percent of the total.
The investments so far have focused on ongoing repairs, replacement of aging equipment, improvement of passenger processing systems, and capacity expansions.
Among its accomplishments are the expansion of terminal curbsides, rehabilitation of power and air-conditioning systems, and upgrading of baggage-handling systems, among others.

“We have made significant progress in less than two years, but there is still a lot more work ahead. Our investments will continue as we modernize NAIA while keeping the airport fully operational,” said Ang.
NNIC said work is now underway on a ground transportation center at Terminal 3, which aims to consolidate and organize transport services around the airport’s busiest terminal.
It is expected to open a new north wing bus gate at Terminal 2 in September, expanding its ability to handle flights at remote aircraft stands while improving the use of available gate capacity.
Apart from expanding Terminals 2 and 3, NNIC is also tasked with rehabilitating Terminal 1 and repurposing Terminal 4 into warehouse and office space.
NNIC is also looking to begin work on Terminal 5, which is set to rise on the former site of the Philippine Village Hotel and is expected to primarily handle domestic carriers.
In terms of operational changes, NNIC has reassigned airlines across the three existing terminals to improve efficiency, in addition to reconfiguring aircraft parking and airside movements.
For the long term, it is looking to enter into airport use agreements with airlines and ground service providers to outline clearer responsibilities and service standards across airport operations.
NNIC most recently secured its first partnership under this new strategy through an agreement with flag carrier Philippine Airlines (PAL).
Taken together, NAIA’s annual passenger capacity is expected to increase to 62 million from the current 35 million over the concession period.
Last year, NAIA’s passenger traffic reached a record high of 52.02 million, according to NNIC.

articles.title: 6 Aeta passengers dead, 3 missing after banca capsizes in Zambales lake
articles.summary: SAN MARCELINO, Zambales — Six members of an Aeta community died while three others remained missing after a motorized banca capsized and submerged in Mapanuepe Lake in Barangay Buhawen here Thursday…

blocks.text: SAN MARCELINO, Zambales — Six members of an Aeta community died while three others remained missing after a motorized banca capsized and submerged in Mapanuepe Lake in Barangay Buhawen here Thursday afternoon, police said.

According to a situation update from Zambales Police Provincial Office director P/Col. Benjamin Ariola, the incident was reported at around 2 p.m. Search, rescue and retrieval operations were immediately launched by personnel of the San Marcelino Municipal Police Station, 2nd Provincial Mobile Force Company, MDRRMO and Bureau of Fire Protection.
Four passengers, including the banca operator, survived the incident.

The six fatalities were identified as Elvie Tiglao Pabalan, Joanavie Mae Tiglao Pabalan, Sally Serrano Dela Cruz, two-year-old Prince Lenard Serrano Dela Cruz, Evelyn Yurik Lagman, and two-year-old Cedric Paanan Liwanag.
Three passengers remain missing: 26-year-old Arlene Paanan Liwanag, who was reported to be pregnant; five-year-old Andrea Serrano Dela Cruz, and 12-year-old Angelito Serrano Liwanag.
All 13 passengers were identified as Aeta residents of Sitio Lumibao, Barangay Sta. Fe, San Marcelino.
The members of the indigenous community were reportedly headed home to Sitio Lumibao after going to Buhawen Proper where they got vaccination shots and attended a 4Ps meeting.
Initial investigation revealed that the banca capsized while traversing the lake reportedly due to overloading.
The recovered bodies were brought to Fama Funeral for proper disposition.
Search and retrieval operations were suspended at around 6:45 p.m. due to inclement weather, and will resume Friday, Aug. 28, as weather and safety conditions permit.
The banca operator remains in police custody as authorities consider the filing of charges for reckless imprudence resulting in multiple homicide.

articles.title: Board of Peace's Gaza envoy criticises Israeli strikes and Hamas actions
articles.summary: Nickolay Mladenov warns that a collapse of last October's ceasefire would be "a point of no return" for the region.

blocks.text: A senior official on US President Donald Trump's Board of Peace has criticised Israel's continuing air strikes on Gaza, as well as the actions of the Palestinian armed group Hamas.
Nickolay Mladenov warned that a collapse of last October's ceasefire would be "a point of no return" for the region.
He was speaking to the UN Security Council after Israel rejected the 15-point roadmap for Hamas's disarmament, which was announced by the Board of Peace last month.
Hamas has agreed to give up its weapons in exchange for a phased Israeli troop withdrawal. But Israel has insisted that the group must fully disarm before any pullout.

At least 1,303 Palestinians, including 300 children, have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since the US-brokered ceasefire began, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
The Israeli military says four of its soldiers have been killed in Palestinian attacks in Gaza over the same period.

The Board of Peace's high representative for Gaza told the Security Council on Wednesday that he and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had agreed at their last meeting on a mechanism through which his government's remaining questions would be settled and that committees had been established for that purpose.
Mladenov said that process had not stalled but warned that risks remained, including the continued killing of Palestinian civilians in Israeli strikes.

"A ceasefire in fact under which civilians are still buried is not yet one that the people of Gaza can really feel. Every use of force that does not answer an immediate threat, and every incident that the deconfliction mechanism was not asked to resolve, costs this process something very hard to buy back," he added.
Mladenov acknowledged that Hamas too had yet to meet fully its commitment to cease all military activities.
"Every weapon carried, every tunnel still worked and every convoy still obstructed sets the process back and hands an argument to those who want to resume war," he said.

He repeated that under the new roadmap, Israeli troop withdrawal from Gaza "follows verified decommissioning" of Hamas weapons handed over to the Palestinian technocratic committee that will govern Gaza under the Board of Peace's supervision.
"It is sequenced and reciprocal," he said.
That is a key difference from comments made by President Trump's envoy, Jared Kushner, after meeting Israel's prime minister two weeks ago.
He said Israeli withdrawal would be discussed only once the demilitarisation of Gaza was "done" - appearing to change the plan in line with Israel's demands.

Israel's representative told the Security Council meeting that it was committed to last October's US-brokered plan for ending the Gaza war, but she insisted it could not succeed while Hamas still had weapons, tunnels and other military infrastructure.
"Disarmament must come first," she stated.
The Palestinian representative said Israel was killing Palestinian civilians with impunity in Gaza and called on the international community to protect them without delay.

Mladenov warned that if the ceasefire was allowed to collapse, "there will be no roadmap to return to, there will be no administration to deploy, and there will be nothing left of the ground to rebuild".
"That would not be a setback. It would be a point of no return for everyone."
The war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.
Israel responded by launching a military campaign in Gaza, during which more than 73,430 people have been killed, according to the territory's health ministry.

blocks.text: The truck that struck a boy and his grandmother in Balamban, Cebu. (Contributed photo)
CEBU CITY — An eight‑year‑old boy died while his 63‑year‑old grandmother was injured after they were hit by a truck in Balamban, Cebu.
Police said the victims were about to cross the road when the accident occurred past 4 p.m. on Wednesday, Aug. 27.
Investigators reported that the driver of a Fuso Canter truck tried to start the engine of the vehicle, which was parked near the town’s public market.
The engine failed to start, prompting the driver to disembark and inspect the battery.
The truck suddenly moved forward and struck the two victims.
Both were rushed to the Cebu Provincial Hospital‑Balamban, where the boy later died.
Police arrested the truck driver following the incident.

articles.title: Cebu health officials probe child’s death after measles-rubella shot
articles.summary: CEBU CITY – Health authorities are investigating the death of a child following a recent measles-rubella (MR) vaccination in Dumanjug, southern Cebu. Dr. Sheila Faciol, chief of the Cebu Provincial…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY – Health authorities are investigating the death of a child following a recent measles-rubella (MR) vaccination in Dumanjug, southern Cebu.
Dr. Sheila Faciol, chief of the Cebu Provincial Health Office (PHO), said a team was immediately deployed to Dumanjug after the child’s death was reported.
“We received the report yesterday and right away today, our team is already in Dumanjug investigating the case,” Faciol said during the Hisgutan Ta! Media Forum on Thursday, Aug. 27.
Faciol said the investigation is expected to yield a report that will help health authorities assess the circumstances surrounding the death.
According to Faciol, the PHO team is gathering information from the Dumanjug Rural Health Unit and Barili District Hospital, where the child was brought.
The Dumanjug Municipal Health Office (MHO) said the child was vaccinated on Aug. 10 and died on Aug. 24, raising concerns about whether the vaccination may have been linked to the death.
The MHO notified the Department of Health Regional Epidemiology and Surveillance Unit and coordinated with both the DOH and PHO for further assessment.
Authorities said the child’s medical records, health condition, and other pertinent circumstances will be examined.
The Dumanjug MHO also appealed to the public to avoid speculation and the spread of unverified claims while the investigation is ongoing.
The incident comes amid rising vaccine hesitancy.
Faciol noted Cebu’s vaccination coverage remains low at 19.7 percent.
“We will not back down. We continue to encourage our mothers to have their children vaccinated,” she said.

articles.title: Thieves steal Bronze Age artefacts from Spanish museum in four-minute heist
articles.summary: The Treasure of Villena is a unique trove of almost ten kilos of gold, bowls, bottles and bracelets dating back to the Bronze Age.

blocks.text: The operation at Villena Museum was "super fast and super professional", a spokesman for Villena town council said.
The city council said the robbery began with a diversion. Around 05:15 local time (03:15 GMT), the alarms went off at the local sports centre, sending police there first, Spanish media reported.
The museum's alarm then went off around 05:20. It took the thieves just four minutes to sweep through museum and leave the building before officers arrived.
The Mayor of Villena, Fulgencio Cerdán, said the thieves "stole a large part of the treasure," specifically all the gold, El Pais reported.
The museum's collection, which dates back to around 1,000 BC, is mainly gold items, but there are also pieces of silver, iron and amber.
It consists of more than 60 bronze age objects, including 29 bracelets, 11 bowls, three bottles and other miscellaneous pieces.
The town is "devastated," Cerdán said. "They've taken most of the treasure."
"I'm even trembling. The truth is that for those of us from Villena, this destroys us. It's part of our heritage, of our wealth," the mayor said.
The collection was discovered in 1963 by archaeologist Jose María Soler in a vessel sunk in a dried-out riverbed in Villena.
The Villena council spokesman insisted there had been "no failure" by the museum.
"All security systems were activated."

The past year has seen a series of raids on European museums. In October 2025, thieves broke into the Louvre museum in Paris in broad daylight, stealing jewellery worth $102m (£75m) before escaping on scooters, in a heist that took about eight minutes.
Last week, four works "of extraordinary value" by Renaissance artist Antonello da Messina were stolen from a museum in Sicily, Italy's culture ministry said.
Earlier this month, Italian police said they had recovered paintings by Renoir, Cezanne and Matisse worth over $10.4m (£7.6m) which were stolen from the Magnani-Rocca Foundation museum near Parma.

articles.title: DILG proposes home inspections for gun safekeeping compliance
articles.summary: ‘This might upset a few people because it might be interpreted as an infringement of rights,’ says Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla during a House budget hearing

blocks.text: CEBU, Philippines – Amid concerns over loose firearm cases following recent school shootings, Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Secretary Jonvic Remulla on Thursday, August 27, said they would propose home inspections to ensure compliance with gun safekeeping protocols.

This happened after Akbayan Representative Dadah Kiram Ismula asked Remulla, during the House hearing into the DILG’s proposed 2027 budget, what the agency has done in response to the school shooting cases in Tacloban City and Zamboanga City, which revealed that the firearms used were owned by uniformed personnel.

“Now, what we are proposing is that the IRR (implementing rules and regulations) has to be amended. The [Philippine National Police] will be granted access to all homes of all lawfully issued firearms to inspect their procedures in safekeeping,” Remulla said.
According to the interior secretary, the minor involved in the Tacloban school shooting took his aunt’s firearm, which was left on a table.

In July, the aunt of the minor told lawmakers during a Senate probe into the Tacloban school shooting that the child broke into her home and forcibly damaged her plastic locker, where she kept her pistol.
In the case of the Zamboanga school shooting, Remulla said that the firearm was simply left in the car, which the shooter was able to take with ease.

“This might upset a few people because it might be interpreted as an infringement of rights. However, we must remember that the privilege to own a gun is not enshrined in our Constitution,” Remulla said.

On Wednesday, August 26, the Philippine National Police (PNP) confirmed that they had filed a complaint for reckless imprudence resulting in homicide and physical injury against the owner of the gun used in the Zamboanga school shooting.

Before this, the Department of Justice had confirmed that Tacloban City prosecutors had recommended the filing of charges for reckless imprudence resulting in multiple homicide and physical injuries against the aunt of the minor involved in the Tacloban school shooting.
Under existing laws, reckless imprudence is a bailable offense.
Remulla recommended lawmakers impose greater penalties against owners of firearms used for illegal purposes.
At present, police are able to check compliance and documents for gun owners applying for or renewing their license to own and possess firearms but are not allowed to conduct home visits.

Remulla said the department is eyeing a revision to the IRR that would allow authorities to inform gun owners that a home inspection would occur and that the said inspection would include a checklist to measure the gun owner’s safekeeping procedures.

“There are over 4 million handguns that are legal in this country, both from uniformed personnel and private owners, so I think it should be the responsibility of the PNP to inspect how they safekeep their guns,” Remulla added. – Rappler.com

articles.title: PH embassy: Consult lawyers as US reviews asylum seekers who entered on short-term visas
articles.summary: 'Filipino nationals who have concerns regarding their current immigration status are strongly encouraged to consult a qualified US immigration attorney,' says the embassy in Washington, D.C.

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – The Philippine embassy in Washington, D.C. urged Filipinos to “remain informed of recent developments in US immigration and visa policies and to ensure compliance with applicable US immigration laws” days after the State Department said it would revoke visas for foreigners who entered the country as short-term visitors and later applied for asylum.
In a statement, State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott confirmed earlier reports about the planned review.

“Obtaining a visa in order to seek asylum is fraud — which is grounds for visa revocation…. These types of visas are issued with the clear understanding that they are for those who intend to return home,” said Pigott.

The State Department, which issues both short-term and long-term visas to the United States, said it will work with the Department of Homeland Security to identify persons who entered the US on short-term visas and later filed asylum to stay for good. The White House, in an X post, said “up to two hundred thousand visas” would be revoked in what it described as the “largest mass visa revocation in history.”

“Recent reports indicate that the US Department of State has begun reviewing B1/B2 business and tourist visas issued to foreign nationals who subsequently applied for asylum in the United States, with visa revocations expected to be undertaken on a rolling basis. Filipino nationals who have concerns regarding their current immigration status are strongly encouraged to consult a qualified US immigration attorney or an accredited legal service provider for advice appropriate to their individual circumstances,” said the Philippine embassy.
It added, “The Embassy reminds the Filipino community that immigration cases are determined by the appropriate US authorities based on the circumstances of each case.”
Filipino nationals may call 202-368-2767 or 202-769-8049, or send an email to atn@phembassy-us.org for consular help and Assistance-to-Nationals concerns, it said.
US President Donald Trump has made immigration and a tough, sometimes brutal, crackdown on those found to have violated immigration laws a cornerstone of his administration.
The State Department said some 175,000 visas had been revoked for various reasons since the second Trump administration started.

The supposed “largest mass visa revocation in history” comes as most polls indicate that Trump’s approval is at an all-time low. Polls have also indicated that Americans, in the lead-up to the midterm elections, have waned in their support of Trump’s war on Iran, on top of growing domestic and economic concerns. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Senate eyes concurrent budget, plenary sessions amid VP trial
articles.summary: Pressed for time, the Senate is eyeing to allow concurrent budget deliberations and plenary sessions to avoid budget delay passage amid Sara Duterte's impeachment trial

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Senators are considering to allow the Senate committee on finance to hold hearings on the proposed P7.2 trillion national budget concurrent with plenary sessions.

Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian announced the move on Thursday, August 27, as the upper chamber formally opened deliberations on the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP) amid the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.
Gatchalian also explained this is to prevent a reenacted budget for 2027.

“We’re going to adjust yung legislative time namin. Papayagan namin ang committee on finance lang magkaroon ng hearing while plenary is in session. Bawal yun eh pero we will suspend the rules for the committee on finance para kahit nagpe-plenary kami, pwede silang mag-hearing,” he said.

(We are going to adjust our legislative time. We will allow the committee on finance to conduct hearings while plenary is in session. That is normally prohibited, but we will suspend the rules for the finance committee so they can hold hearings during plenary.)

The finance committee is considering conducting the budget hearings starting the second week of September from Mondays to Fridays, according to the Senate chief. However, the panel will hold the deliberations on afternoons of Mondays to Wednesdays to accommodate the impeachment trial.

“Kapag impeachment mahirap yun, kailangan andito ang senator-judges. But with plenary, magiging flexible kami para mahabol ng committee on finance ang schedule dahil ngayon kalahating araw [ang] na-take up na ng impeachment so wala nang time ang commmittee to conduct the hearings,” Gatchalian added.

(It is difficult during an impeachment trial because senator-judges need to be present. But with regular plenary, we can be flexible so the committee on finance can catch up on its schedule. Half of our day is currently taken up by the impeachment, leaving the committee no time to hold budget hearings.) – Rappler.com

articles.title: Man who attacked nun on CCTV in Jerusalem acquitted on grounds of mental health
articles.summary: A Jerusalem court said the Jewish attacker was having a psychotic episode when he assaulted the nun, in an incident which caused outrage.

blocks.text: An Israeli court has acquitted a Jewish man who attacked a nun in Jerusalem, in an incident caught on CCTV which drew widespread condemnation.

Jerusalem Magistrates Court said Yona Schreiber was experiencing a psychotic episode when he pushed over and kicked the French nun in the Old City in occupied East Jerusalem in April. It ruled that he was not criminally responsible for his actions and ordered him to be sent to a psychiatric hospital for up to six years.
Video of the attack caused outrage, and deepened concerns after a rise in harassment of Christian clergy and pilgrims by Jewish extremists in the Old City.
The victim, who hit her head on a stone block, suffered a bruised face and leg.
Schreiber, 36, had been charged with assault motivated by hostility towards a religious group.
According to the district psychiatrist's report, Schreiber "was in a psychotic state at the time of the act and is not substantively fit to stand trial".
The prosecution accepted the psychiatrist's opinion and asked for Schreiber to be acquitted and committed to hospital.
Judge Ofir Tishler said that although Schrieber had attacked the nun, he was ordering his acquittal due to his mental health.
At the time of the attack, the French Consulate in Jerusalem said it strongly condemned Schreiber's "aggression".
The director of the French Biblical and Archaeological School, where the nun is a researcher, called the assault an "act of sectarian violence".

Israel's foreign ministry denounced the attack, calling it a "shameful act [which] stands in direct contradiction to the values of respect, coexistence, and religious freedom upon which Israel is founded and to which it remains deeply committed."

"Israel remains firmly committed to safeguarding freedom of religion and freedom of worship for all faiths, and to ensuring that Jerusalem remains a city where every community can live, pray, and practice its faith in safety and dignity," the ministry said on X.

While the violence of the attack on the nun is unusual, in the past few years in Jerusalem's Old City there have been regular cases of religious Jews spitting and acting aggressively towards those wearing Christian religious dress or symbols.

Church properties have been vandalised and there have also been bitter disputes caused by settler takeovers. Church leaders accuse Israel of trying to change the status quo – long-standing agreements on ownership and responsibilities - at their holy places.

A 2025 report by the Rossing Center, a Jerusalem-based organisation which aims to foster better inter-faith relations in the Holy Land, describes a "recent surge in overt animosity towards Christianity", putting this down to "a continued deepening of polarisation and ultra-nationalist political trends".

articles.title: Join Rappler Movers Program: Write stories, build communities of action

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines Do you want to be a community storyteller or lead advocacies in your locality?

For more than a decade, Rappler Movers have used storytelling and community action to amplify local issues, spark conversations, and help create change. Movers are volunteers of Rappler representing various provinces and regions in the Philippines committed to amplify stories and promote civic action at the local level.
Since 2012, the program has connected community storytellers, advocates, and leaders nationwide through MovePH, Rappler’s civic engagement arm.

Now, MovePH is strengthening this nationwide community to create more opportunities for Movers through its new Movers Program to stay connected, learn from one another, and bring meaningful change wherever they are.

The program aims to build a long-term community where Movers can stay connected with Rappler, continue developing their skills, collaborate with fellow Movers nationwide, and find opportunities to contribute to stories and initiatives that matter.
In this community, Movers choose their own path. Whether they’re a natural-born storyteller or a driven community organizer, there’s a place for Movers to lead, create, and make an impact.
As community storytellers, Movers can:

items: Write or report stories from their community and surface issues, people, and perspectives that deserve attention
Build skills in journalism, news writing, digital storytelling, fact-checking, and community reporting
Pitch stories and get feedback from Rappler editors, journalists, and data experts

blocks.text: As community organizers, Movers can:

items: Help bring people together around issues that matter to your community
Participate in or help organize campaigns, discussions, and community initiatives
Build skills in community engagement, organizing, and civic action

blocks.text: Movers can also do both — use storytelling to help communities engage with issues and highlight local voices, and community organizing to turn those conversations into action.
Through the program, Movers will have opportunities to:

items: Build their skills through training from Rappler’s learning arm, RappLearn
Get mentorship from Rappler editors, journalists, data experts, and community engagement specialists, among others
Connect and collaborate with Movers from different communities and regions
Participate in a Movers’ Leadership Program, an exclusive hybrid training for Movers, as part of MovePH’s roadshows in selected areas as they become available
Take on leadership roles, including opportunities for committed Movers to lead a local Movers hub and help organize storytelling and community engagement activities locally
Explore other opportunities within Rappler, including internships, journalism fellowships, special projects, article contributions, and other pathways for growth and continued involvement

blocks.text: The Movers network continues to grow across the Philippines, with eight hubs currently in Iloilo, Iligan, Batangas, Metro Manila, Zamboanga, Pangasinan, Dumaguete, and Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).
The program is open year-round for applications of new and aspiring young Movers.
Specifically, aspiring Movers must be or have:

items: At least 18 years old and based in the Philippines
Affiliated with a local student or civil society organization
Strong writing and communication skills
Proven experience in community leadership/organizing or local storytelling
Committed to long-term civic engagement volunteering
Can attend monthly meetings or activities

Submissions will be reviewed at the end of each month, and applicants will receive an update after each review cycle. Shortlisted applicants must complete the onboarding process.

articles.title: Southwest monsoon affecting Luzon, Western Visayas; LPA inside PAR may strengthen
articles.summary: (1st UPDATE) PAGASA says the low pressure area has a 'medium' chance of developing into a tropical depression, but it is still the southwest monsoon or 'habagat' that is mainly affecting Luzon and…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – A new low pressure area (LPA), which entered the Philippine Area of Responsibility on Thursday morning, August 27, has a “medium” chance of developing into a tropical depression.

The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said this LPA — the ninth LPA in August alone — was last located at 850 kilometers east of extreme Northern Luzon.
Once it develops into a tropical depression, it will be called the local name Pilandok.

“Hindi pa ganoong kalaki ang impluwensya [ng LPA] dahil hindi pa pronounced ‘yung paghila niya sa habagat. Ang main na nakakaapekto pa rin po sa atin ay itong hanging habagat,” PAGASA Weather Specialist John Manalo said during their 5 pm forecast on Thursday.
(The LPA does not have much influence yet because its pull on the southwest monsoon is not yet as pronounced. What’s mainly affecting us is still the southwest monsoon.)

The southwest monsoon or habagat is bringing occasional rain to Benguet, La Union, Pangasinan, Zambales, Bataan, and Occidental Mindoro, and scattered rain and thunderstorms to Metro Manila, the rest of Luzon, Western Visayas, and Negros Island Region.

articles.title: Collapsed glacier likely caused devastating Nepal-Tibet floods, scientists say
articles.summary: Preliminary investigations by scientists have pointed to a collapsed glacier as the cause, highlighting the issue of rapidly melting Himalayan ice.

blocks.text: Aerial footage shows floods on Nepal-Tibet border

Preliminary investigations have pointed to a collapsed glacier as the cause of the flash flood on the Nepal-Tibet border, highlighting the issue of rapidly melting Himalayan ice, scientists have told the BBC.
Initial reports of an earthquake led many to believe that a tremor had caused a landslide, which in turn caused the flood that has killed at least 389 people.
However, the US Geological Survey then clarified that the disaster was caused by a "glacial collapse", which is when a glacier or part of a glacier disintegrates.
The impact of the collapsed glacier hitting the bottom of a valley was so powerful that it registered a magnitude of 5.2, according to USGS data and scientists who have analysed the event.

Dr Simon Cook, a glacier expert with the University of Dundee, told the BBC his team had detected that the lower part of a glacier in Nepal near the Langtang Lirung peak - which is approximately 15km (9 miles) west of the site of the floods - had collapsed.
He estimated that the glacier collapsed in a northwesterly direction and then travelled westwards downstream.

blocks.caption: BBC graphic showing how a glacier collapse sent ice and rock debris into a river between Tibet and Nepal

blocks.text: An analysis , externalby the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), an intergovernmental scientific institution, found there could have been "an ice-rock avalanche originating from a high-altitude area".

This caused a "large volume of ice and rock debris" to enter the Lende Khola, a tributary of the Bhote Koshi river, which in turn generated a sudden surge in the river carrying water, sediment and large boulders downstream.
The centre found that water levels in rivers downstream rose by between seven and nine metres within a span of 30 minutes, and several water monitoring stations were washed away or damaged.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Scientists say a collapsed glacier near the Langtang Lirung peak likely caused the disaster

blocks.text: Image source, Getty Images
Scientists say a collapsed glacier near the Langtang Lirung peak likely caused the disaster
Mike Searle, a professor of earth sciences at Oxford University, said that this whole process - from landslide to flood - could have taken hours or even days.
"The sheer wave of debris suggests there could have been a landslide first; the water built up, dammed the river, and then it burst in one huge great flood," he told the BBC.

The topography of the area could have also exacerbated the flood. Searle pointed out that Langtang Lirung sits on the crest of the high Himalayas and there are "incredibly steep valleys" on both sides of the mountain, which could have funnelled the water at higher speeds.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Images from the scene show the steep sides of the affected valley

blocks.text: Image source, Reuters
Images from the scene show the steep sides of the affected valley
It is still unclear what caused the glacier to collapse on Wednesday.

Searle said that Langtang Lirung, like the rest of the Himalayas, has been slowly rising due to long-term tectonic movement, where one plate has been pushing another plate up. "It's like putting a jack under the car, and then jacking it up."
"As the mountain is rising, the glacier gets steeper and steeper, and it's inevitable that parts of it fall off."

But usually these are smaller chunks which temporarily block the rivers, and are easily flushed out, he said. However, in this disaster, the whole glacier seems to have collapsed "in one go", which Searle said is "very unusual". "These floods happen all the time, but not at this scale."

He said Wednesday's event likely happened because of "two different processes - tectonics with the Himalayas uplifting, and then climate change with increasingly high temperatures and melting of glaciers.
"The whole thing is combining to form these catastrophic disasters that we are now seeing at a regular basis."
Scientists for years have warned of melting ice and permafrost, which is centuries-old frozen soil, in the Himalayas due to climate change.

One analysis released by ICIMOD, external earlier this year found that the Hindu Kush Himalaya glaciers are now losing ice at double the rate since 2000. This in turn exacerbates dangers such as flooding.
Dr Cook pointed out that there have been similar incidents of floods and landslides caused by glacier collapses in India, Switzerland and Italy in recent years.

In 2021, a large chunk of a Himalayan glacier collapsed in the valley of Chamoli in northern India, sending a cascade of debris and water downstream that killed 200 people. Scientists later estimated that the impact of the collapse was equivalent to 15 atomic bombs.
Even in Nepal, the same region saw flooding last year caused by a glacial lake in Tibet bursting.

blocks.caption: Aerial images showing a before and after of the Trishuli river on 23 and 26 August. In the second photo, brown sediment can be seen spilling out over the banks.

blocks.text: Mohd Farooq Azam, a specialist with ICIMOD, said the increasing frequency of hazards in the cryosphere - or the frozen parts of the Earth - "is becoming more visible than ever before. The pace of change is so rapid."
While it is difficult to say whether any single event is caused by climate change, "when you look at the pattern of these events, you do think climate change could have an impact," said Dr Cook.

"The logic is that with a warming planet, you will see shrinking glaciers, lots of snow melt. The permafrost that is partially holding some mountainsides together is warming and thawing and degrading."
"So you are going to get more landslides, debris flows, glacial meltwater, lake outbursts, glacier collapses, because climate warming ultimately destabilises these high mountain environments."

articles.title: 'The flood took everything': Nepal survivors describe horror of loved ones being swept away
articles.summary: One woman says her father, mother, sister and sister's children were carried away before her eyes.
articles.byline: Shaktimaya Tamang, Shreejana Shrestha, Gabriela Pomeroy

blocks.text: Survivors of massive flash floods in Nepal have recounted how they saw their loved ones disappear into torrents of mud.

At least 389 people have died and 900 others are missing after floods wiped out entire villages on the border of Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday, with a force so powerful seismologists initially identified it as an earthquake.
Rescuers trudged through thick mud and debris on Thursday as Nepalese authorities rushed to bring aid and relief supplies to the affected areas.
"My family members were swept away by the flood in front of my eyes," Kalpana Malla from Nepal's Nuwakot district told the BBC.
Malla said her father, mother, sister and sister's children were all claimed by the disaster.
"They could not escape the flood; there was no chance at all," she said. "This flood took everything, but my son and I climbed the rooftop of a house and survived but couldn't explain how."
Her son, Sugam Malla, said he saved his mother by pulling her hand.
He said he had given his phone to his sister so she could keep in touch, but the mobile was no longer reachable.
"I am worried she must be swept away."
Another woman, Goma Pandit, said she had lost her buffaloes and all her other cattle.
"My farmland is also swept away. Ten sacks of mustard seeds, tons of corn and rice paddy are all gone. Nothing is left."
At Kathmandu's TU Teaching Hospital, families of those missing in the floods wait anxiously for updates.
Holding up her phone, Ram Khumari Shrestha says: "This is my husband. He was off to Rasuwa as a part of his driving job. He was in contact with me until 8 pm yesterday.
"But I couldn't call him this morning. The phone was switched off," she told the BBC.
Mani Shrestha Bishwa was also camped out at the hospital on Wednesday night, hoping to hear from his younger brother, cousin, uncle and friend.
"I last contacted them at 8:30 in the morning," he said.
Trekking guide Sonam Dorjee missed the flood in his home village of Rasiwa Syafru by about an hour. He had left at 08:00 local time.
As he was driving to Kathmandu, Dorjee told the BBC he had heard the sound of floods gushing into their village.
"It [sounded] like an earthquake," he said. "My house has collapsed... I have seen a photo."
Dorjee said his sister, Dechen Tamang, was missing, along with her husband and several other family members.
He described the flood as "sudden and devastating".
"Many survivors are now left without homes and they need emergency rescue and evacuation, as well as food, temporary accommodation and medical support."
He is praying his sister is found alive. "There is a 10% chance, we hope," he said.

At least 160 were killed and hundreds are missing in the wake of the disaster Wednesday morning.

Video from the Chinese side shows a raging wall of mud and debris crashing over a building several stories high, engulfing it and sweeping away buses and cars like they are toys.
It is too soon to draw any firm links to climate change, but there are well-documented trends in the “Roof of the World” that have increased the likelihood of such hazards.
Landslide, then tremors, says USGS
Nepal’s Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal said an earthquake likely triggered a landslide that in turn blocked a river, sending water gushing downstream after it eventually breached the obstruction.

But in a new note, the US Geological Survey said that while the event was initially reported as a magnitude 4.4 earthquake, “additional analysis of long period seismic waves indicate that the seismic energy was instead generated by a landslide.”

Hatim Sharif, a hydrologist at the University of Texas San Antonio, told AFP one thing that struck him was the lack of rainfall beforehand.
“That defeats essentially every operational flood warning system in the world,” he said.
Running won’t help
By the time you see the mud flow coming, it’s too late, said Sharif.
“Running will not help,” nor will trying to flee by vehicle, Sharif added, because the mud and water moving at high speed form a lethal combination “like liquid concrete.”
The only solution is to climb up a hill, at least 20 feet (six meters), he estimates.
One possible long-term remedy might be river level gauges that relay changes to authorities in real-time, giving residents 20-30 minutes of warning, he said.
Dorothy Heinrich, a researcher at the UK’s University of Reading, told AFP: “In these mountain environments, the rivers can be quite narrow in areas.”
Anything that blocks them, be it an avalanche or landslide, will lead to a “big accumulation of water, then it creates these incredibly fast floods.”

Nepal is also prone to glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) — the sudden and catastrophic release of vast volumes of water from melting glacier-fed lakes.
One such catastrophe in July 2025 originated in China’s Gyirong County, then surged into Nepal’s Rasuwa District, though authorities have not yet said a GLOF was responsible for the latest event.

In the coming days and weeks scientists around the world will be investigating potential climate links through what are known as attribution studies, which analyze how likely an event was in the fossil-fuel-warmed climate of today, versus the pre-industrial era.

Tibet government officials mobilized nearly 800 emergency workers and 150 vehicles as well as sniffer dogs and speed boats to help the rescue efforts, China’s official Xinhua news agency said.
In the area hit by the disaster, rescuers waded through mud and sludge to look for survivors after floodwaters buried the lower floors of multi-storey buildings.

Some 403 tourists — 341 of them foreigners — were unaccounted for several hours after the disaster struck, according to Nepal’s tourism ministry.

“Entire villages and market areas have been wiped out,” said David Fisher, the Nepal head of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC).
It said it was was dispatching emergency supplies including blankets, first aid kits, stretchers and body bags.

Locals were traumatised, while experts cautioned that a lingering blockage in a river could produce an additional flood.

Images shared by Nepali police showed floodwater surging through a river, sweeping away houses in its path, while AFP images depicted the top floor of a house sticking out from muddy soil.
The Nepali Army was carrying out flights and had rescued scores of people, while others living near the river in danger zones had been told to relocate.
